== on strings compares C pointers, not text (gcc warns: "comparison with string literal results in unspecified behavior"). The input S holds the text "hi" but not the literal's address, so S == "hi" is false. t was set from an identical literal, so t == "hi" is true, as is "x" == "x". copy == null is true; then copy = S.
isNull is now false; copy = "ho". S == "hi" is false whatever the text.
